result_text:
**The claim doesn't hold.** For mobile, returning users in the evening peak on 2026-07-15, p95 checkout latency was about 439 ms, below 500 ms.

I treated this as one claim to check, with no rival explanations to sort out.

**The claimed segment**
- **Result:** 71 requests, p95 = 438.6 ms, 95% bootstrap interval 397–468 ms. 500 ms is outside that interval, so the check is conclusive.
- **Tail:** only 1 of the 71 requests exceeded 500 ms (598 ms).
- **Robustness:** the result holds for other evening windows (17–21, 19–23, 17–24, 20–24 UTC). p95 ranged from 408 to 434 ms, and every upper bound stayed at or below 468 ms.

**The "only" part also fails.** The slow slice is mobile, new users, in the evening:
- **Evening, mobile, new users:** p95 = 804 ms (interval 510–867 ms), with 9 of 63 requests over 500 ms.
- **Whole day:** p95 = 453 ms (interval 433–472 ms), so there was no overall exceedance.
- **All evening traffic:** p95 = 497 ms, with a wide interval of 468–633 ms.

The mobile, new-user finding came from looking at the data after the claim was tested, so treat it as a lead rather than a finding. Mobile new users are also slow outside the evening (p95 = 552 ms, interval 479–626 ms), so this may be general slowness for that group rather than an evening effect. I can't separate the two from this data.

**Limits**
- "Evening peak" wasn't defined and the timestamps are UTC, so I assumed 18:00–21:59 UTC and checked the alternative windows above.
- Traffic is flat at one request per minute, so the data shows no peak of its own.
- The file ends at 23:19, so the last 40 minutes of the day are missing. I can't tell whether that is an export gap.
- Each segment's p95 rests on only a few slow requests, so the intervals are wide.

The ledger is in `/var/folders/4_/s6fbcjyn4b13xdxkd3lv0kw00000gn/T/arm-s13-pre-amvg147s/work/ledger.md`, with probe outputs in `probe_a.txt` and `probe_b.txt` in the same folder.
